# Curves and subdivision fixtures

The car embeds the control points, indexed face-varying UVs, faces and 314 authored crease edges of Pixar's OpenSubdiv `catmark_car.obj`, with separate wheels added for presentation. The source OBJ (with trailing whitespace normalized) and OpenSubdiv license and notice are in `source/`. The subdivision playground and specimen groups embed the cages, subdivision schemes, crease/corner values and hole tags from `subd-modelling/examples/subdivision-study/scene.subd`; its original model is retained in `source/scene.subd`. Individual specimens are translated for framing, while the playground keeps their arrangement. Materials and presentation differ from the original modeling application.

Six NURBS patches and six sets of NURBS curves use cubic, multiple-span knot vectors; one of each has nonuniform rational weights. These are compact authored controls rather than pre-tessellated mesh replacements. Recreate the suite with `python3 usd-wasm/scripts/generate-curved-surfaces-fixtures.py`; it reopens each stage and checks its schema, control counts, knot counts, and relevant authored features. The gallery requests high subdivision complexity.

Native Storm 26.05's NURBS adapter may show control-cage approximations rather than evaluated rational surfaces or curves. NURBS cards use `scripts/nurbs_reference.py` to evaluate rational basis functions into a temporary native mesh or linear-curve proxy, then render it with Storm; the capture index records that provenance. A successful stage open or a visible preview does not establish full USD feature support.
